## About
Dan's Automotive Repairs, LLC is a full service foreign auto repair shop in Branchburg, New Jersey. We handle everything your car needs, from routine maintenance to more complex repairs, on European cars with a special focus on Volkswagen and Audi. If you have a domestic car, we will take care of it as well.
We know where these cars tend to fail: valve cover gaskets and camshaft oil seals that leak, carbon build-up on the intake valves of TSI and TFSI engines, timing chain tensioners that wear out. Knowing the common causes lets us assess problems quickly and accurately, then explain what is going on and what it takes to fix it.
Customers rate the shop 4.8 from 74 Google reviews. Reviewers describe Dan as honest and straightforward, and say he tells you what your car actually needs before any work goes ahead.

## Services
- Volkswagen: Service, maintenance and major repairs on Volkswagens. German cars are our specialty.
- Audi: Maintenance and repair for your Audi, including the known issues on TFSI engines.
- Manufacturer Scheduled Maintenance: Service at the mileage intervals your manufacturer recommends, to extend the life and optimize the performance of your European car.
- Engine diagnostic & repair: Check engine lights, rough starts, misfires and oil consumption, diagnosed and repaired.
- Brake repair: Brake inspection and repair as part of regular maintenance.
- Heating & A/C: Heating and air conditioning repair.
- Tune-ups: Tune-ups to keep the engine running smooth.

## FAQ
Q: Do you work on domestic cars?
A: Yes. We specialize in European cars, especially Volkswagen and Audi, and we take care of domestic cars as well.

Q: Can I just drop in?
A: It's best to call ahead. One reviewer notes the shop is busy and recommends booking an appointment in advance rather than expecting work done the day you show up.

Q: What are your hours?
A: Monday through Friday, 8:00 AM to 5:00 PM. Closed Saturday and Sunday.

Q: Does my TFSI engine need a new timing chain tensioner?
A: Almost every TFSI engine made between 2008 and 2013 came with bad timing chain tensioners. If yours hasn't been updated, or you don't know, have it replaced before it causes catastrophic engine damage.

Q: My car is leaking oil or smells like burning oil. Where should I look?
A: Have the valve cover gaskets and camshaft oil seals checked. Those are the most common spots for leaks. Schedule an appointment and we'll diagnose it.
